hash_distributed_join_with_aggregates.comment: Tests join correctness when both inputs are already hash-distributed on the join keys via aggregation thus resulting in a pre-partitioned distribution.

queries.description: Join with aggregation on both sides - exercises hash-distributed exchange routing
queries.sql: SELECT l.key_col, l.sum_val, r.sum_metric FROM (SELECT key_col, SUM(value_col) AS sum_val FROM {left_tbl} GROUP BY key_col) l JOIN (SELECT key_col, SUM(metric_col) AS sum_metric FROM {right_tbl} GROUP BY key_col) r ON l.key_col = r.key_col ORDER BY l.key_col

queries.description: Count joined rows with aggregated inputs
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT key_col, SUM(value_col) AS sum_val FROM {left_tbl} GROUP BY key_col) l JOIN (SELECT key_col, SUM(metric_col) AS sum_metric FROM {right_tbl} GROUP BY key_col) r ON l.key_col = r.key_col

SELECT SUM(l.sum_val), SUM(r.sum_metric) FROM (SELECT key_col, SUM(value_col) AS sum_val FROM {left_tbl} GROUP BY key_col) l JOIN (SELECT key_col, SUM(metric_col) AS sum_metric FROM {right_tbl} GROUP BY key_col) r ON l.key_col = r.key_col

queries.description: Direct join with same group keys as join keys
queries.sql: SELECT a.key_col, SUM(a.value_col), SUM(b.metric_col) FROM {left_tbl} a JOIN {right_tbl} b ON a.key_col = b.key_col GROUP BY a.key_col ORDER BY a.key_col

multi_table_join_chain.comment: Tests join chains that create multiple hash-distributed exchanges

queries.sql: SELECT c.name, r.region, SUM(o.amount) as total FROM {orders} o JOIN {customers} c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN {regions} r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.name, r.region ORDER BY c.name
SELECT c.name, o.total_amount FROM {customers} c JOIN (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) as total_amount FROM {orders} GROUP BY customer_id) o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id ORDER BY c.name

join_with_mv_filter.comment: ARRAY_TO_MV filters in WHERE must be pushed below the join to the leaf stage, the only stage that can run them. An MV predicate matches a row if any value matches.

queries.description: ARRAY_TO_MV equality with another conjunct on the same side
queries.sql: SELECT o.order_id, c.name FROM {orders} o JOIN {customers} c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'open' AND ARRAY_TO_MV(o.tags) = 'urgent' ORDER BY o.order_id

queries.description: Two ARRAY_TO_MV equalities on the same column are not folded to false
queries.sql: SELECT o.order_id, c.name FROM {orders} o JOIN {customers} c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE ARRAY_TO_MV(o.tags) = 'urgent' AND ARRAY_TO_MV(o.tags) = 'vip' ORDER BY o.order_id

queries.description: ARRAY_TO_MV IN filter with a filter on the other side and an aggregate above the join
queries.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM {orders} o JOIN {customers} c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE ARRAY_TO_MV(o.tags) IN ('urgent', 'vip') AND c.name <> 'Charlie' GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name
